cards.text: In visions of God, the prophet Ezekiel has been brought to the land of Israel (Ezekiel 40:2). Now the Lord GOD tells him how to divide the land as an inheritance among the twelve tribes of Israel. Friend, if you've ever tried to split ONE bill TWELVE ways, you know this is gonna take some planning.

cards.question: God is dividing the land among the twelve tribes, but one name gets two portions. Who is it?
God tells the tribes to divide the land equally among them.
Why does God say this land will fall to Israel as an inheritance?

answers.text: He swore to give it to their forefathers
They won it back from their enemies
They paid for it with silver and gold

cards.text: Then God marks out the borders on all four sides, from the Great Sea in the west to the Jordan in the east, and from up by Damascus and Hamath in the north down to the Brook of Egypt in the south. Friend, neighbors stop SPEAKING to each other over one foot of fence, and here God just draws the whole map Himself, no surveyor, no arguments.
God says to divide the land among the tribes of Israel. But hold on. He's not done with the guest list yet.

cards.question: Besides the tribes of Israel, who does God say gets an inheritance in the land?
God says to treat the foreigners who live among them as ___ Israelites.
A foreigner has to take his inheritance in a special area set aside just for foreigners.

cards.text: Then God names the tribes, one strip each running east to west, lined up from the north: Dan, Asher, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, Reuben and Judah. Manasseh and Ephraim are Joseph's two sons (Genesis 41:51-52), and each one gets a strip of his own.
Right below Judah comes a strip God says to set apart. And something sits right at its center.

cards.question: What sits at the center of the strip God tells them to set apart?

cards.text: Part of it is a holy portion for the priests, 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 wide. And God doesn't just hand it to ANY priest. He's got a list, and He checked it.

cards.question: Which priests does God give this holy portion to?
God says the descendants of Zadok went astray along with the rest of the Israelites.

cards.text: Zadok was a priest back in King David's day (2 Samuel 8:17). God says Zadok's descendants kept His charge, but the Levites went astray when the Israelites did.
God calls the priests' land a most holy portion. Right next to it, the Levites get a strip the exact same size, 25,000 by 10,000.

cards.question: The Levites must not ___ or exchange any of their land, because it is ___ to the LORD.

cards.text: What's left goes to the city, with houses, pastureland, and fields on both sides whose produce feeds the city's workers. You work the land and the land feeds you back, friend, and THAT is a benefits package I'd update my résumé for.

cards.question: The workers who farm the city's land all come from the tribe of Judah.

cards.text: Put the holy portion and the city land together and you get a perfect square, 25,000 cubits by 25,000 cubits. But there's still land left on both sides of that square, running all the way out to the borders.

cards.question: The land on both sides of the holy portion and the city will belong to the ___.

cards.text: That prince is the ruler over God's people in this vision (Ezekiel 45:8-9). Below the middle section, the rest of the tribes line up to the south, one strip each: Benjamin, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, and Gad at the bottom, down along the Brook of Egypt.

cards.question: The city gets twelve gates, three on each side. What does God name the gates after?

cards.text: North side gates: Reuben, Judah, and Levi, and Levi wasn't even in that list of tribal strips. That's like not getting a parking spot at work and then seeing your name on the front of the BUILDING.

cards.question: Joseph got two portions of land, so the city gives him two gates as well.
The city's perimeter runs 18,000 cubits. From that day on, what will the city's name be?

cards.text: All those borders, all those cubits, and it all lands on one name. Most towns get named after a river, a king, or some guy who planted a flag and refused to leave, but this city gets named for Who is THERE.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Levi" could be argued right. In this passage Levi's descendants get two portions of the holy district: the priests' portion for Zadok's descendants (48:10-11) and the Levites' portion beside it (48:13). A baker could pick Levi and defend it. Replace it with a tribe that clearly gets one portion, such as Reuben or Dan.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The joke about splitting ONE bill TWELVE ways suggests an even split. That hands the baker the answer to card 3, which asks whether the land is divided equally (47:14). Change the comparison so it doesn't hint at equal shares.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card is three sentences: "God says to divide the land among the tribes of Israel.", "But hold on." and "He's not done with the guest list yet."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card is three sentences: the holy portion's size, "And God doesn't just hand it to ANY priest." and "He's got a list, and He checked it."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "workers" could be argued right. In 48:18 the land bordering the holy portion on the east and west supplies food for the city's workers, and stop 2 card 9 already told the baker about "fields on both sides whose produce feeds the city's workers." The question says only "the land on both sides of the holy portion and the city." It never says this land lies outside the 25,000-cubit square and runs out to the borders, so the context the baker needs lives only on card 11, which is no longer on screen. Add that context to the question, or replace "workers."

rule.text: If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The parking-spot joke suggests Levi was left with nothing, then honored with a gate. But the Levites do get land: a strip the same size as the priests' (48:13), as stop 2 card 7 already told the baker. Levi only lacks a tribal strip. The comparison blurs that fact. Rework it so the joke is about not being on the list of tribal strips, not about getting no land at all.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it.
